channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Water-utility attacks are still spreading — FBI cites “at least seven states,” later reporting puts it near a dozen
item.description: The coordinated campaign against water and wastewater OT that began 26–27 July has not stopped. On 30 July the FBI and EPA issued a public-service alert — and CISA a companion “significant escalation” warning — confirming malicious actors struck internet-facing controllers in at least seven states, changing the IP addresses and passwords on exposed Rockwell Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100/1400 PLCs and cutting remote monitoring and control. By 5 August reporting (Bloomberg, Fortune) said the activity was continuing and the tally had grown toward a dozen states. Disclosed OT-affected utilities now include 30+ Minnesota systems — Braham’s well and treatment plant were briefly shut down, and Plymouth, South St. Paul and Maple Plain also reported incidents — nine systems in Michigan and a wastewater lift station in Rapid City, South Dakota; many ran on manual control. Researchers assess Iran-linked CyberAv3ngers as the likely actor, possibly abusing the unpatched Rockwell flaw CVE-2021-22681, but the US government has not formally attributed it and the FBI investigation is ongoing. No utility has reported contaminated drinking water. - FBI/EPA PSA & CISA alert / NBC News, Bloomberg, Fortune — FBI confirmed, attribution pending - Attacks since 27 Jul 2026 — FBI/EPA/CISA alerts 30 Jul; still ongoing per 5 Aug reporting

item.title: [High] Iran-affiliated actors are manipulating water-system PLC logic (AA26-097A, updated 22 Jul)
item.description: The mechanism behind the Minnesota disruption is spelled out in advisory AA26-097A, updated 22 July. Federal agencies confirm Iran-affiliated actors are reaching internet-exposed PLCs — Unitronics, Rockwell and, newly, Schneider Modicon and Siemens S7-1200 — using the same engineering software legitimate operators use, extracting project files, and rewriting or deleting control logic. In some cases they disabled shutdown and alarm functions so equipment can drift into unsafe states without alerting staff. The update documents project-file exfiltration for the first time and adds detection guidance for tampering with reusable code modules. For a small utility the exposed devices are ordinary dosing, pump and lift-station controllers left reachable with default or shared passwords. - CISA/FBI/NSA/EPA joint advisory AA26-097A - Updated 22 Jul 2026 (originally 7 Apr 2026) — ongoing

item.title: [High] FSB Center 16 router campaign (AA26-194A): exposed edge gear in front of municipal water SCADA
item.description: A joint advisory from NSA, CISA, the FBI and ~12 partner nations (AA26-194A, 13 July) details how Russia’s FSB Center 16 — Static Tundra / Berserk Bear / Energetic Bear / Dragonfly — scans for devices exposing SNMP with default community strings and abuses Cisco Smart Install to copy device configs. State and local government is named explicitly, which is what most municipal water utilities are. The same internet-facing edge routers sit in front of treatment-plant and lift-station SCADA, and a stolen config is a ready-made map before an intruder touches a controller. - NSA/CISA/FBI joint advisory AA26-194A - Published 13 Jul 2026 — ongoing

item.title: [High] Researchers tie the water attacks to CyberAv3ngers and an unpatchable Rockwell flaw
item.description: Analysis from Tenable, Dragos and others points at Iran’s IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers as the likely hand behind the Minnesota and multi-state disruptions, though the government has not formally attributed them. The suspected route is CVE-2021-22681, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication-bypass in Rockwell Logix controllers with no vendor patch (Rockwell offers only defense-in-depth mitigations) — a long-standing entry in CISA’s KEV catalog. The same crew earlier hijacked 75+ Unitronics Vision PLCs at water utilities using the default ‘1111’ password. The pattern is consistent: internet-exposed, weakly-authenticated controllers, chosen for public visibility rather than a single vendor bug. Treat any exposed Rockwell, Unitronics, Schneider or Siemens controller as in-scope regardless of utility size. - CVE-2021-22681 - Reporting through 5 Aug 2026 — attribution pending

item.title: [Critical] Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day (CVSS 10) exploited — added to CISA KEV
item.description: CISA added Arista’s VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw CVE-2026-16812 (CVSS 10.0) to the KEV catalog on 27 July after it was exploited as a zero-day. It is an unauthenticated OS command-injection bug in on-prem VCO — the console that manages VeloCloud SD-WAN edges — needing only network reach to the web interface, with a 30 July federal fix deadline. Multi-site water utilities increasingly use SD-WAN to link plants, tanks and lift stations, so a compromised orchestrator is a direct path toward the OT network. CISA added a second flaw the same day, Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 (CVSS 5.3, information exposure), which requires prior file-system access. - CVE-2026-16812 - Added to KEV 27 Jul 2026 — actively exploited

item.title: [High] Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center zero-day exploited — hard-coded password on the IT/OT boundary
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-20316 to the KEV catalog on 29 July after Cisco confirmed active exploitation before a patch existed. The flaw is a hard-coded password in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (formerly Firepower Management Center) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker log in with a low-privilege account and read sensitive data — firewall rules, VPN configs, device inventory and event logs. That console often governs the firewalls separating a utility’s IT from its plant OT, so even limited access is valuable reconnaissance for lateral movement toward SCADA. Any water utility running FMC should patch and pull its management interface off the internet. - CVE-2026-20316 - Added to KEV 29 Jul 2026 — actively exploited

item.title: [Info] EPA’s 2026 National Cyber Drill tests whether water still flows when the network doesn’t
item.description: The EPA launched its 2026 National Cybersecurity Drill challenging drinking-water and wastewater utilities to keep critical functions running when telecom and internet access are degraded or gone. The scenario forces operations in a “disconnected” state — limited or no SCADA remote connectivity, cloud services, email or VoIP — to test manual fallback and sector resilience. Participation is a low-cost way to pressure-test whether a utility can run blind. - US EPA / Industrial Cyber - 2026 National Cyber Drill — Jul 2026

item.title: [Info] Congress temporarily extends water cyber authorities as EPA issues new guidance
item.description: Congress temporarily extended lapsing water-sector cybersecurity legal authorities while the EPA released new guidance for utilities, keeping the federal support structure in place amid ongoing debate over a permanent regulatory model for water. For utilities the practical signal is continuity: baseline expectations and available federal resources remain, and permanent requirements may still be coming. - Nossaman / EPA - Jul 2026
